title: Convergent pin-selector client resolution and telemetry for model versioning
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Define and implement client-side pin selector resolution semantics across tag, semver range, and commit-hash selectors; add lightweight telemetry hooks so clients and server can observe resolution outcomes and fallbacks. Goal is deterministic resolution that surfaces explainability and helps runtime choose compatible variants without surprise regressions.
background: We onboard a growing number of community models with multiple version identifiers (tags like 'stable', semver ranges, and opaque commit hashes). Server-only resolution has led to surprising runtime fallbacks when capacity or compatibility constraints occur and limited visibility for SDK users. Multiple internal issues reference caller confusion and undiagnosed regressions when model variants change. This ticket standardizes a client-side resolution API to make selector intent explicit and observable.
proposal: Add a deterministic client-side resolution library in the SDKs and a minimal canonical resolution algorithm surfaced by the API. Key principles: 1) deterministic precedence order that can be configured per-request, 2) explicit opt-in for 'best-effort' (allow runtime to pick a compatible variant) vs 'strict' (exact selector only), 3) emit telemetry events for resolution decisions and fallback reasons, 4) server will continue to validate and may override resolution if strictly incompatible and will return structured explanation headers. The client library will also provide a 'preview' call to ask the control plane which exact model ref would be chosen for a selector list without executing inference.
api_changes:
- New request-level field: 'pin_selectors': list of selector strings (examples: 'tag:stable', 'semver:>=1.2.0 <2.0.0', 'hash:3f2a1b'), and optional 'selector_mode' enum: {strict, convergent, permissive}.
- New header: X-RW-Resolution-Preview to request preview response.
- New telemetry flags: resolution.exact_match, resolution.fallback_taken, resolution.reason.
- SDK: add PinResolver.resolve(selectors, mode) -> resolutionDecision (string) and PinResolver.preview(selectors) -> promisedRef (string).
resolution_algorithm_overview: 1) Normalize selectors into typed entries (tag, semver-range, hash). 2) If any hash selector present and mode==strict -> attempt exact hash match first. 3) In convergent mode: compute candidate set by intersecting selectors semantically; if intersection empty, expand candidates by relaxing semver ranges (widen patch -> minor -> major) up to a configurable window. 4) Apply performance_profile filter: prefer candidates with published profiles that match the request's target latency/cost profile. 5) Tie-break deterministically: highest stabilityScore then newest publish_date then lexicographic artifact id. 6) If no candidate remains and permissive mode enabled, fallback to 'closest-compatible' model type (e.g., smaller quantized variant) and emit fallback telemetry.
acceptance_criteria:
- SDKs expose PinResolver.resolve and preview APIs with unit and integration tests.
- Server responds to preview header with deterministic ref and explanation.
- Telemetry events emitted for 100% of resolution flow and accessible in Console.
- Migration path documented and deprecation warnings emitted for legacy implicit pinning in responses.
- No user-facing regression in primary e2e nightly test matrix for existing workloads.
testing_plan: Unit tests for selector normalization, semver expansion, and tie-break logic. Integration tests: local SDK -> staging control plane preview roundtrip, mock fallbacks when performance profile mismatch. Load test: ensure preview header scale and that telemetry emission cost is bounded. Add golden test cases for commonly ambiguous selector combos from internal corpus. QA checklist attached in links.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement SDK previews and telemetry in canary SDK build; 2) Server support for preview header behind feature flag; 3) Rollout SDK changes to beta customers for opt-in; 4) After 3-week feedback window, flip default 'convergent' behavior on for new SDKs and keep legacy implicit behavior for older SDK versions with deprecation header; 5) After 3 months, deprecate legacy path and enforce preview-first behavior. Monitoring to include user error rate, increase in fallback events, and model-quality regression alerts.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive semver relaxation could surface unintended regressions. Mitigation: require performance_profile match for relaxed candidates and prefer published performance profiles; also gate relaxation behind a 'relaxation_window' config. Risk: telemetry volume spikes. Mitigation: batch telemetry with sampling and only emit full reason fields for sampled events. Risk: client-server divergence. Mitigation: server continues to validate final choice and returns structured explanation; SDK preview ensures parity before call.
